notes: Single source of truth for FreeCAD host support. Read by dcc_mcp_freecad.compat (service side) and by freecad_driver.py (inside FreeCAD's interpreter). A version outside `supported_ranges` is rejected explicitly; it is never silently downgraded. Each breaking change names the tools it limits in `affected_tools`; an `unused` break names none, because the adapter never calls the moved API. get_capabilities reads that list, so the capability declaration and the guard cannot disagree.

supported_ranges.evidence: Real FreeCAD 1.0.2 end-to-end run in CI: create/add/update/transform/boolean/validate/inspect/export STEP+STL/import/save_copy/remove, plus scale/copy/mirror, the wedge and helix primitives, and 3MF export - 40 passed / 0 skipped. Wedge and helix geometry and the 3MF millimetre unit declaration are measured against the request on this line, not merely reported.

Real FreeCAD 1.1.4 end-to-end run in CI: the same end-to-end path plus scale/copy/mirror, the wedge and helix primitives, and 3MF export - 40 passed / 0 skipped. No adapter-visible API break: the Part/Placement/boolean/MeshPart surface used by the driver is unchanged, and the wedge, helix and 3MF measurements agree with the 1.0.x line.

breaking_changes.title: Sketcher constraint property `Symmetric` renamed to `Midplane`

probe.pre_change_note: A freshly added Sketcher::SketchObject on real FreeCAD 1.0.2 does not expose Symmetric as an instance attribute either, so the pre-change presence claim is recorded as unverified instead of being assumed.

breaking_changes.symptom: Sketch constraints set through the old property name are dropped; the document recomputes as if the constraint never existed, so the tool reports success while the geometry stays wrong.
breaking_changes.remediation: Use `Midplane` on FreeCAD 1.1+; keep the `Symmetric` spelling only on 1.0.x.

breaking_changes.title: Sketcher `ExternalGeometryCount` removed

probe.pre_change_note: A freshly added Sketcher::SketchObject on real FreeCAD 1.0.2 does not expose ExternalGeometryCount as an instance attribute either, so the pre-change presence claim is recorded as unverified instead of being assumed.

breaking_changes.symptom: Reading the count returns nothing instead of a number, so sketch bookkeeping silently reports zero external references.

breaking_changes.title: PartDesign feature reversal property moved: `Symmetric` -> `Midplane` -> `SideType`

probe.pre_change_note: Neither the pre-change nor the post-change presence is asserted: which spelling a given build exposes is exactly what this probe measures. Both expectations stay unverified until a real host has reported them, so the matrix records evidence instead of a guess.

breaking_changes.symptom: Writing the reversal property under the wrong generation's name is dropped, so a two-sided pad is computed one-sided and the feature still reports success.
breaking_changes.remediation: The adapter resolves the property by capability, trying `SideType`, then `Midplane`, then `Symmetric`, and refuses when a host exposes none of them instead of writing to a name that silently does nothing.

breaking_changes.title: MeshPart tessellation (`meshFromShape`) deflection behaviour changed
breaking_changes.replacement: MeshPart.meshFromShape with an explicitly asserted mesh result
breaking_changes.symptom: Tessellation honours deflection differently, so an STL/OBJ export can succeed with an empty or degenerate mesh instead of failing.
breaking_changes.remediation: The adapter asserts the tessellated mesh is non-empty and bounded before exporting: an empty mesh, or one whose bounding box is missing or not finite, raises an explicit error naming the host version instead of writing a plausible-looking file.
